title: Zieliński Tadeusz Andrzej
name: Zieliński Tadeusz Andrzej
description: musicologist, music critic, composer; b. 22nd May 1931 in Warsaw; d. 25th February 2012 in Warsaw. He was born in a family of famous musicians. His grandfather Bolesław Domaniewski – pianist, teacher and composer – was a principal of the pre-war Fryderyk Chopin State Higher School of Music in Warsaw. His mother Zofia was a pianist, his father – a violinist by passion – was a military officer. Genealogical connections even point to the Mikuli family (Tadeusz’s great-grandmother was a great-granddaughter of Karol Miuli, a student of Chopin) and Chopin himself through the Czachowski and Mikuli family (P. Mysłakowski, Wśród krewnych I powinowatych Chopina [ Among Chopin's relatives and in-laws ], “Ruch Muzyczny” 2012 No. 2; TA Zieliński, “Ruch Muzyczny” 2012 No. 5). In 1957 he graduated from musicology studies under the supervision of Zofia Lissa at the Institute of Musicology at the University of Warsaw. At the same time, he took private harmony and counterpoint classes with Piotr Rytel. A thorough knowledge of the composer’s language benefited his musical writing. He started his professional career in 1957 in the Polish Radio editorial office, first in the third and then in the second channel. Until 1981, he hosted a series of programmes on Polish and European 20th-century music, which are a compendium of knowledge about the most outstanding artists and their musical styles. In the years 1960–1991 he was an editor and author of the bi-weekly “Ruch Muzyczny”. He published numerous articles in Polish and foreign magazines, including German "Melos", Swedish "Nutida Musik", "Nuova Revista Musicale Italiana", and "Musica America". His musicological publications, articles and monographs are devoted to the life and work of Fryderyk Chopin and to contemporary music, including the work of Polish composers. Many of them were translated into foreign languages and received important prizes, including the Hungarian medal for the monograph on Bela Bartók, the medal of the Minister of Culture for the book about Karol Szymanowski. The monograph on Chopin, which is one of the most extensive studies of this type in Chopin literature in the second half of the 20th century, received the French publishers 'Prix des Muses' award in 1996. For many years, Tadeusz A. Zieliński commented on music of renowned Polish composers such as Witold Lutosławski, Andrzej Panufnik, Grażyna Bacewicz, Kazimierz Serocki, Tadeusz Baird, Włodzimierz Kotoński, Andrzej Dobrowolski, Krzysztof Penderecki, Henryk Mikołaj Górecki, Krzysztof Meyer, Roman Maciejewski, Juliusz Łuciuk, Marta Ptaszyńska and others. Apart from music, his second passion was philosophy. His philosophy books were published under the pseudonym Antoni Domaniewski: Byt i względność (Warsaw 2002), Homo domini. Mały traktat etyczny (Warsaw 2008) and Osiem zagadek świata (Warsaw 2014). In 2002, Tadeusz A. Zieliński received the Polish Composers' Union Award "for outstanding musicological and critical achievements in the field of contemporary music", and in 2006 – the annual award of the Minister of Culture and National Heritage "in the field of music". updated: 2020 (ac) SELECTED LITERATURE Kofin Ewa Czy harmonika może być naturalna?
